title: More than one electron
blurb: Two honest models I keep of the same atom, and the size of their disagreement.

steps.title: My cheap model: pretend the nucleus is weaker
body: In a screened central field I replace the other electrons with a fitted reduction of the nuclear charge. It is fast, it is APPROXIMATION, and I took its parameters from a 1974 paper.
It works well enough to be worth having and badly enough to be worth checking, which is what I do in the next step.

steps.title: My honest one: solve for the field
body: In Hartree-Fock I give every subshell its own field and iterate until the field and the orbitals agree. I fit nothing.
I get sodium's ionization energy near 4.95 eV against a measured 5.14. The gap is correlation, which this model of mine does not have, and I state that gap rather than tuning it away.

steps.title: Atoms my cheap model cannot do at all
body: Sulfur and chlorine have no published screening parameters, so I cannot draw them with the fitted model. Hartree-Fock needs none and I solve them from scratch.
I move you to Hartree-Fock rather than offering a model that would refuse every request, which is the difference between a limit and a bug.

steps.title: Both, on one axis
body: The total radial density is the one thing both of my models claim to describe, so it is the one place I can compare them without arguing about conventions.
I draw the disagreement rather than describing it. Where the curves separate is where the fitted model is spending its error.
